displayContract.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that a carefully bounded cumulative inference from categorical authority, basic moral knowledge, transformative aspiration, and rational fulfillment can modestly favor classical theism when compared against fully specified secular alternatives.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the live case by joining its comparative framework, limited conclusion, and authority account while explicitly requiring developed rival comparison.

premises.text: At least some moral judgments present themselves not merely as efficient means toward chosen ends but as requirements applying even when compliance frustrates immediate self-interest.

novelty.explanation: This develops the transcript distinction between categorical obligation and instrumental assessment without asserting that phenomenology alone settles its ontology.

premises.text: A personal ground is explanatorily relevant only if moral perfection constrains that ground independently and if moral access includes publicly discussable defeaters and correction procedures.

novelty.explanation: This repairs candidate specification and access by adding independent constraints, fallibility, and correction rather than relying on an idealized divine description.

premises.text: Properly basic moral beliefs can supply provisional knowledge when they survive reflection, role reversal, factual correction, and comparison with coherent counterexamples.

novelty.explanation: This adds defeater-sensitive reliability conditions to the transcript's properly basic moral knowledge proposal.

premises.text: Transformative aspiration contributes evidence only when defined as a stable orientation toward moral repair, not as an unsupported expectation of literal perfection.

novelty.explanation: This narrows the disputed transformation horizon into a defensible phenomenon while preserving ordinary secular mechanisms.

premises.text: Theistic support should increase only when one integrated account explains categorical authority, fallible knowledge, correction, and long-range hope more economically than combined secular accounts.

novelty.explanation: This incorporates the bad-lot objection and requires comparison against combinations of secular explanations rather than isolated alternatives.

conclusion.text: Accordingly, the moral evidence can provide limited comparative support for classical theism only if these access, specification, reliability, and candidate-pool conditions are independently met.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion strengthens the bounded inference by making its most important unresolved conditions explicit.

newArguments.title: Normative convergence under correction
newArguments.text: Convergence becomes more evidentially interesting when it persists after factual education, reciprocal role reversal, exposure to unfamiliar interests, and removal of self-serving distortions. Such convergence would not prove a divine source, but it could support the claim that moral cognition tracks constraints deeper than local preference. The theistic case could then ask whether a morally perfect personal ground explains both authority and corrigible access better than secular rivals, while remaining answerable to comparative evidence.

novelty.explanation: This is a genuinely new line using convergence under controlled correction as potential comparative evidence rather than treating ordinary agreement as decisive.

newArguments.title: Relational clarity compatibility test
newArguments.text: A relational account of hiddenness should predict enough noncoercive clarity for responsible moral agency while leaving relationship freely chosen. Theism therefore gains credibility only if it can explain a middle range between overwhelming manifestation and harmful ambiguity: accessible moral reasons, corrigible traditions, and opportunities for sincere response without compelled affection. This framework converts a vague appeal to divine priorities into a comparative prediction and acknowledges that persistent destructive confusion would count against the hypothesis.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the relational reply by specifying a testable middle-range expectation that directly addresses clarification, access, and harm.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that moral experience currently supports disciplined secular inquiry more strongly than a theistic inference because natural mechanisms explain substantial phenomena while divine candidacy, access, discrimination, and hiddenness remain unresolved.

novelty.explanation: This consolidates the strongest secular objections into a proportionate undercutting thesis rather than claiming that secular accounts settle every metaethical question.

premises.text: Ordinary moral change, conscience, and substantial ethical convergence have plausible natural pathways through learning, empathy, reciprocal reasoning, institutions, and shared creaturely vulnerability.

novelty.explanation: This develops the transcript's separate secular mechanisms into an integrated and explicitly pluralistic explanatory account.

premises.text: Goal-relative assessment can be objective after foundational commitments are stated, although the commitments themselves remain open to public criticism, expansion, and revision.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the well-being account by abandoning the claim that no further normativity appears and permitting principled revision and broader scope.

premises.text: A supernatural candidate should be admitted to comparison when it has discriminating content and evidential consequences, without requiring deductive proof or experimental reproduction.

novelty.explanation: This replaces an overly demanding demonstrability standard with one appropriate to comparative abductive reasoning.

premises.text: Divine grounding supplies limited epistemic benefit unless people can identify the relevant deity, distinguish genuine requirements from projection, and correct harmful interpretive errors.

novelty.explanation: This develops the access objection while preserving the distinction between an ontological foundation and practical moral knowledge.

premises.text: Comparative confidence should remain modest whenever multiple secular mechanisms can operate jointly and the broader candidate pool has not been representatively developed.

novelty.explanation: This applies the candidate-pool constraint to combined explanations while respecting the affirmative's expressly limited conclusion.

conclusion.text: Accordingly, the available moral phenomena warrant continued secular explanation and methodological caution, while withholding a positive theistic inference unless candidacy, access, and comparative discrimination improve.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion proportionately favors withholding the inference rather than asserting that naturalism or secular metaethics has been conclusively established.

newArguments.title: Error-correction advantage
newArguments.text: An explanatory framework should be evaluated partly by its procedures for detecting and correcting moral error. Secular inquiry can compare outcomes, expose affected parties' testimony, revise institutions, and test whether principles survive reciprocal scrutiny. These procedures are imperfect, but their failures are publicly inspectable. A divine-command interpretation adds value only if it improves correction rather than multiplying disputed authorities. This criterion shifts comparison from the mere existence of moral convictions toward the reliability of practices that revise them.

novelty.explanation: This introduces public error correction as an independent comparative criterion rather than restating empathy, well-being, or divine access alone.

newArguments.title: Explanatory decomposition
newArguments.text: The four moral phenomena need not share one ultimate explanation. Authority judgments, knowledge, transformation, and rational motivation may arise from partially independent social, cognitive, biological, and philosophical processes. A single theistic hypothesis gains no automatic economy merely by labeling all four effects together; it must outperform a decomposed secular model on fit, constraints, and error prediction. This approach also prevents failure in one secular mechanism from being treated as evidence that every component requires the same supernatural source.

novelty.explanation: This is a genuinely new argument that challenges the assumption that the four explananda should receive one unified underlying explanation.
